notes: 先尝试出声，再按需查看中英答案；每题单独记状态。

questions.title: Clothing
questions.text: Do you wear different styles of clothes on weekdays and weekends?
questions.english: I'd keep a similar casual style on weekdays and weekends. The occasion matters more than the day, so I'd dress differently for a meeting rather than simply because it's Monday.
questions.chinese: 工作日和周末我会保持相近的休闲风格。场合比日期更重要，所以我会为会议换穿着，而不只是因为周一。
pending: 该偏好或习惯为完整候选，待确认是否符合本人。

questions.title: Clothing
questions.text: What colour clothes do you like?
questions.english: I'd choose darker colours like navy or grey because they're easy to combine. I prefer a simple overall look to bright colours that attract lots of attention.
questions.chinese: 我会选藏蓝或灰色等深色，因为容易搭配。比起引人注意的亮色，我更喜欢简单的整体样子。
pending: 该偏好或习惯为完整候选，待确认是否符合本人。

questions.title: Jokes & Comedies
questions.text: Are you good at telling jokes?
questions.english: I'm fairly quiet at first, so I don't constantly tell jokes. With people I know well, I'd be more likely to make a light comment that fits the conversation.
questions.chinese: 我一开始比较安静，所以不会不停讲笑话。和熟人在一起时，我更可能说些符合谈话情境的轻松玩笑。
pending: 性格真实；讲笑话方式为候选。

questions.title: Jokes & Comedies
questions.text: Do your friends like to tell jokes?
questions.english: Some friends enjoy making jokes during casual conversations. I prefer that natural kind of humour to prepared jokes, because it feels more connected to what we're talking about.
questions.chinese: 有些朋友喜欢闲聊时开玩笑。我更喜欢这种自然幽默，而不是准备好的笑话，因为它与当时的话题更相关。
pending: 朋友幽默习惯为授权候选，非已确认观察。

questions.title: Jokes & Comedies
questions.text: Do you like to watch comedies?
questions.english: Yes, especially ones with clever dialogue. I'd watch a comedy to relax, but I prefer humour that feels natural rather than actors constantly shouting or exaggerating.
questions.chinese: 喜欢，尤其是对白巧妙的。我会看喜剧放松，但更喜欢自然幽默，而不是演员不停大喊或夸张表演。
pending: 该偏好或习惯为完整候选，待确认是否符合本人。

questions.title: Jokes & Comedies
questions.text: Have you ever watched a live show?
questions.english: Yes, I once watched a small student performance. It wasn't professionally produced, but the audience's laughter made it feel more lively than watching a recording at home.
questions.chinese: 看过，我曾看过小型学生演出。虽然不是专业制作，但观众笑声让它比在家看录像更有现场感。
pending: 学生演出为完整候选经历，时间地点未知。

questions.title: Jokes & Comedies
questions.text: Are comedy shows popular in your country?
questions.english: Yes, comedy is popular in films and online videos. Short clips are easy to watch during a break, although different audiences enjoy quite different styles of humour.
questions.chinese: 受欢迎，电影和网络视频中的喜剧很流行。休息时看短片很方便，不过不同观众喜欢很不同的幽默风格。

questions.title: Headphones
questions.text: Do you use headphones?
questions.english: I'd use headphones when watching anime without disturbing others. Since I live with my mother, that would be a considerate way to enjoy something on my computer.
questions.chinese: 我会在看动漫又不想打扰别人时用耳机。我和母亲同住，所以这是用电脑娱乐时体贴的做法。
pending: 动漫与同住者真实；耳机习惯为候选。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text:
Describe a person who loves to grow plants (e.g. vegetables, flowers) at home or in
the garden
You should say:
Who this person is
What plants he/she grows
How he/she grows the plants
And explain why he/she loves growing plants
questions.english:
A person who enjoys growing plants is my mother. We live together in an apartment in Guangdong, where a few small pots can fit comfortably.

She grows mint and a few flowering plants near a window where they can receive light. The plants aren't arranged as a perfect display. She pays attention to each one, checks the soil, and changes the position of a pot if it seems to need more sunlight.

Her approach is patient and practical. She waters them when necessary rather than following a rigid rule every day. When a plant produces new leaves, she notices the change and enjoys seeing that her care has made a difference. The routine is small, but it gives the room a more lively atmosphere.

I think she likes growing plants because it offers a calm activity with visible progress. Unlike many tasks on a computer, the result develops slowly and can't simply be rushed. I enjoy technology, so I find that contrast interesting. It also shows how someone can create a little contact with nature without needing a house or a large outdoor space.
questions.chinese:
喜欢种植物的一个人是我的母亲。我们一起住在广东的一套公寓里，屋里可以摆下几个小花盆。

她在能够晒到阳光的窗边种了薄荷和几盆开花的植物。她并没有把这些植物布置成一套完美的陈列，而是会留意每一盆的状态，检查土壤；如果某盆植物似乎需要更多阳光，她就会挪动它的位置。

她照料植物的方式很耐心，也很实际。她在植物需要时浇水，而不是每天机械地遵循同一个规则。当植物长出新叶，她会注意到变化，也很高兴看到自己的照料起了作用。这只是一个小小的日常习惯，却让房间更有生气。

我觉得她喜欢种植物，是因为这是一项安静的活动，而且能看到进展。与许多电脑上的任务不同，植物的变化慢慢发生，不能简单地催促。我喜欢技术，所以觉得这种对比很有趣。这也说明，即使没有独栋房子或很大的户外空间，人们仍然可以与自然建立一点联系。
pending: 母亲同住广东公寓已确认；种植爱好、薄荷花卉、窗边摆放、照料方式和动机全部为授权候选。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text:
Describe a new law you would like to introduce in your country
You should say:
What law it is
What changes this law brings
Whether this new law will be popular
How you came up with the new law
And explain how you feel about this new law
questions.english:
A new law I would like to propose is a stronger, simpler requirement for apps to explain and limit their use of personal data. China already has privacy rules, so I wouldn't describe privacy protection as a completely new idea.

The additional requirement would be a standard permission screen written in clear language. An app would have to explain what information it needs, why it needs it, and how users can withdraw permission. Refusing unnecessary access shouldn't prevent someone from using the basic service.

I think this could make people more confident about using technology. It might be popular with users who feel confused by long terms and conditions, although some companies could dislike the extra work. Proper enforcement would matter as much as the wording of the law.

The idea came from thinking about how easily people click through permission requests without understanding them. As an AI student, I'm interested in useful systems, but usefulness shouldn't depend on collecting everything possible. I would feel positive about a rule that makes the choices clear and keeps data collection proportionate. It would help technology serve people while allowing them more control over their own information.
questions.chinese:
我想提议的一项新法律，是要求应用以更有力、更简单的方式说明并限制个人数据的使用。中国已经有隐私保护规则，因此我不会把隐私保护说成一个全新的想法。

我希望新增的要求，是一个使用清晰语言的标准权限页面。应用必须解释需要哪些信息、为什么需要，以及用户怎样撤回授权。用户拒绝不必要的访问权限，不应妨碍他们使用基本服务。

我认为，这可能让人们更有信心使用技术。它也许会受到那些被冗长条款弄得一头雾水的用户欢迎，不过一些公司可能不喜欢由此增加的工作。法律能否得到切实执行，与条文本身同样重要。

这个想法来自我的思考：人们很容易在并不理解权限请求的情况下，直接点击通过。作为人工智能专业的学生，我对有用的系统感兴趣，但系统有用不应该以尽可能收集所有信息为前提。我会支持让选择更清楚、让数据收集保持适度的规则。这样既能让技术服务于人，也能让人们更好地掌控自己的信息。
pending: 这是一项观点提案，非现行法条解读或真实政策；用户是否持此观点待确认，不声称中国完全没有相关法律。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: What kinds of occasions need people to arrive early?
questions.english: Flights, job interviews and important examinations are obvious examples. Arriving early gives people time to find the right place and deal with unexpected delays. It can also show respect when others are waiting. I would allow a reasonable buffer, though, rather than arrive so early that I interrupt preparations or make the host uncomfortable.
questions.chinese: 乘飞机、求职面试和重要考试都是明显的例子。提前到达让人有时间找到正确地点、应对意外延误，也能体现对等候者的尊重。不过，我会留出合理的缓冲时间，而不是早到打断准备工作，或让主人不自在。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: Why do some people like to stay up late?
questions.english: Some people feel more alert at night, especially when the surroundings become quiet. Others stay up because of work, entertainment or conversations with friends. The problem is not simply the clock time, but whether their schedule allows enough sleep. Staying up late regularly becomes unhealthy if they still have to get up very early.
questions.chinese: 有些人晚上更清醒，尤其是在周围安静下来后。另一些人则因为工作、娱乐或与朋友聊天而熬夜。问题不只是睡觉的钟点，而是作息能否保证充足睡眠。如果仍需很早起床，长期晚睡就不健康。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: Is it good to arrive early in any situation?
questions.english: Not in every situation. Being early is sensible for an examination or a train, because missing it has clear consequences. But arriving much earlier than agreed at someone's home may inconvenience the host. I think punctuality means considering the situation and other people's schedules, not always trying to be the first person there.
questions.chinese: 并非任何场合都适合。考试或赶火车时提前到达很合理，因为错过会有明确后果。但去别人家时比约定早很多，可能会给主人添麻烦。我认为守时应考虑具体情况和他人的安排，而不是总想第一个到。

questions.title: 早起经历
questions.text: What kind of people like getting up early?
questions.english: People who enjoy a quiet start or have regular morning commitments may prefer it. For example, someone who exercises before work can make that activity part of a routine. However, I would not link early rising automatically with success. Different people have different energy patterns, and getting sufficient sleep matters more than copying someone else's timetable.
questions.chinese: 喜欢安静开局、或早晨有固定安排的人，可能偏好早起。例如，在上班前运动的人，可以把运动纳入固定作息。不过，我不会把早起自动等同于成功。每个人的精力规律不同，睡够比照搬他人的时间表更重要。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: What are the advantages of growing vegetables or flowers at home?
questions.english: Growing plants can make a home more attractive and give people a relaxing activity away from screens. Vegetables may also provide a small amount of fresh food. For children, watching a plant grow makes patience and responsibility easier to understand. It takes space and care, though, so the benefits depend on what a household can manage.
questions.chinese: 种植物可以让家更好看，也提供远离屏幕、放松身心的活动。蔬菜还能带来少量新鲜食物。对孩子而言，观察植物生长让耐心和责任感更容易理解。不过，种植需要空间和照料，收益取决于家庭能够承担的程度。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Do many people grow vegetables or flowers at home in your country?
questions.english: Some people in China do grow flowers or vegetables at home, but the available space makes a big difference. A house with a garden allows larger plants, while apartment residents might keep a few pots on a balcony. I would not claim that everyone does it; personal interest, time and sunlight all affect the choice.
questions.chinese: 中国确实有人在家种花或种菜，但可用空间影响很大。有花园的房子能种较大的植物，公寓居民可能只在阳台放几个花盆。我不会说人人都这样做，个人兴趣、时间和光照都会影响选择。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Is it easy to grow plants at home?
questions.english: It depends on the plant and the conditions at home. A hardy plant can be fairly easy to keep if it has enough light and appropriate watering. Growing vegetables successfully may take more attention. Beginners should start with something manageable rather than buy many plants at once, because regular care matters more than initial enthusiasm.
questions.chinese: 这取决于植物以及家里的环境。耐养的植物只要光线和浇水合适，就比较容易养。想成功种出蔬菜可能需要更多照料。新手应从容易管理的植物开始，而不是一次买很多，因为持续照料比最初的热情更重要。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Why do some people like to grow plants?
questions.english: For some people, it is a relaxing hobby with a visible result. They can watch something develop gradually instead of dealing only with tasks on a screen. Others enjoy making their surroundings greener or sharing vegetables with family. The attraction is not necessarily saving money; caring for a living thing can be rewarding in itself.
questions.chinese: 对一些人而言，这是有可见成果的放松爱好。他们可以观察事物逐渐生长，而不是只处理屏幕上的任务。也有人喜欢让环境更绿，或与家人分享蔬菜。吸引力未必在于省钱，照料生命本身就可能让人有满足感。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Why do some people prefer to grow their own fruits and vegetables instead of buying them from the market?
questions.english: They may value freshness and enjoy knowing how their food was grown. It can also be satisfying to eat something they have cared for themselves. However, home growing does not automatically mean cheaper or safer food. People still need suitable soil, water and sensible methods, so I see it as both a hobby and a practical activity.
questions.chinese: 他们可能看重新鲜度，也喜欢了解食物的种植过程。吃到自己照料长成的食物，还会有满足感。不过，自己种不自动意味着更便宜或更安全，仍需合适的土壤、水和合理方法。因此，我认为它兼具爱好和实用活动的性质。

questions.title: 喜欢在家/花园种菜的人
questions.text: Do you think students should learn to grow plant?
questions.english: Yes, a small growing project can teach students where food comes from and why living things need care. It also gives science lessons a practical side. Schools do not need a large garden; a few suitable containers could work. The aim should be understanding and responsibility, rather than expecting every student to become an expert gardener.
questions.chinese: 可以。小型种植项目能让学生了解食物来源，以及生命为什么需要照料，也让科学课更贴近实践。学校不必有大花园，几个合适的容器就能尝试。目标应是理解和责任感，而不是让每位学生都成为园艺专家。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text: What rules should students follow at school?
questions.english: Students should follow rules that protect learning and safety, such as arriving on time, treating others respectfully and doing their own work. Rules against bullying are particularly important. However, schools should explain the reasons instead of demanding blind obedience. Students are more likely to take a rule seriously when they understand whom it protects.
questions.chinese: 学生应遵守维护学习和安全的规则，比如准时到校、尊重他人、独立完成作业。禁止欺凌尤其重要。不过，学校应解释理由，而不是要求盲目服从。学生理解规则在保护谁时，更可能认真遵守。

questions.title: 想颁布的新法律
questions.text: Do people in your country usually obey the law?
questions.english: I think people generally try to follow the law, although compliance varies with the situation. Clear rules and fair enforcement make cooperation easier. Some violations happen through carelessness or a lack of understanding, while others are deliberate. Rather than make a claim about everyone, I would focus on improving legal awareness and making enforcement consistent.
questions.chinese: 我认为人们通常愿意守法，但遵守情况因情境而异。清晰的规则和公平执法有助于配合。有些违法源于粗心或不了解规定，也有些是故意的。与其概括所有人，我更关注提升法律意识和保持执法一致。
